page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 with dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 124.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. The storage subsystem consists of two local NVMe SSDs totaling 539 GB of capacity. No GPU resources are included on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core execution and text processing, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and a text processing score of 2913.0. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are strong, with gzip compression reaching 36.02 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.11 GB/sec. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall within the average range, showing a stress-ng multi-core score of 17938.08 and large-block memory read bandwidth of 133.46 GB/sec. Small-model LLM text generation is highly efficient at 366.16 tokens/sec, though larger model inference scales down to average tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside integrated local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for IOPS-heavy workloads. However, the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, and multi-threaded scaling remains in the average tier compared to higher-core configurations. This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive databases, text processing pipelines, caching layers such as Redis, and software compilation tasks.
